title: Judge the set as well as each item
statement: Check a bank, form or course as a set as well as item by item: find repeats, near-duplicates and items that give away, prime or contradict one another.
example: 65 of 76 lesson bundles scored exactly 0 on a quality judge's check for repeats.
detail: A quality judge's bundle-level check found repeats inside most lessons: non-repetitiveness averaged 0.14, and 65 of 76 bundles scored exactly 0 on it (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0083-clone-lessons-inceptbench-results-2026-07-02-eval-summary.qmd`). A Grade 3 course passed that judge's item-level evaluation but not its holistic course-level one (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0076-coe-catchup-2026-06-30.qmd`), and a live test form whose items were bound to an unrelated passage was recorded as the kind of defect that passes item evals and fails the course eval (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0234-misc-artifacts-gate-eval-checks-recovery.qmd`). In one review round a single word pair cracked the usage checks on two forms (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0211-peter-pan-reviewer-round-2708.qmd`), and the project's routing rules make answer position, option length, distractor function, enemy items, blueprints and independent cold review obligations of the form (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`). Check answer positions, option lengths, key spread and coverage across the set, and keep parallel forms disjoint.
against: the notes on those results say the zeros on multi-passage bundles say more about how the bundles were packaged for the judge than about their content (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0083-clone-lessons-inceptbench-results-2026-07-02-eval-summary.qmd`, line 94). The set was training data, not items shown to students, and the first fix was a five-row spot check, with a structural audit still to be added (the data session's `HANDOVER.md`, line 287). In that certifier, non-leakage across items was grep-verified per item at authoring time, with a full automated collision check still pending (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/COURSE_QUALITY_GATE_REPORT.md`, line 398).

Cueing enemies: one item's stem or options give away the answer to another.
Redundancy enemies: two items test the same narrow content, distorting the blueprint.
Contradiction enemies: two items present inconsistent information, confusing the student.
have at least two people review the assembled assessment specifically for these relationships.
A preceding item defines “opportunity cost,” making the next item easier; fine for an in-lesson quiz, risky for “stable mastery” claims.
For generalisable mastery claims, avoid strong primes or move them out of proximity
